verses.mystical_translation: A new voice in the south lifts its standard in the days of a northern king.
Brief rule under a mother's name; the land is rent by arms.
Two hosts like mountains face each other; numbers thunder though their meaning can waver.
From a high place a speech unrolls like a banner into the valley.
A covenant of enduring taste: salt that seasons rule and memory.
A servant rises and the circle is broken—authority made a field of contest.
Where firmness fails, empty men gather to seize the empty place.
A people's multitude and an idol's glitter confront the claim of covenantal rule.
A sacrificial market: whoever pays is made priest of the not-God.
A people who keep the service stand under the name that made them.
Morning and evening the quiet work of presence keeps a thin thread to the holy.
The captain is not a man but the Presence; the blast is a summons and a denunciation.
Betrayal surrounds—the line has two fronts.
They turn and find themselves encircled; a single cry rises and the silver mouths answer.
The shout converts the moment; a blow falls like a consequence of prayer and cry.
Flight becomes the hinge upon which the victory turns.
A field of silence after the roar—countless fallen, named by a number that echoes judgment.
Prevailing is attributed to reliance—a theological reading of the outcome.
Taken towns mark the map of shifting hands; names hold memory and dispute.
A life that will not gather strength returns to the quiet of death by divine strike.
Might multiplies into households and names—a private proliferation after public war.
What the book leaves aside, the prophet keeps in the quiet registry of memory.

contemplative_note: Power, ritual, and legitimacy clash here; listen for the trumpet as both summons and judgment.
